# Write a friendly product description with DeepSeek

> **In short:** With DeepSeek, you describe what you're selling in plain words and get a short, persuasive listing back. The free version is enough for this task, and you'll spend about 15 minutes total.

If you sell anything online — candles, prints, software, cookies, used books — you need a product description that actually makes people want to buy. Most of us stare at a blank box and write three boring sentences. DeepSeek, a free AI assistant you can use in your browser, can turn the basic facts about your product into friendly copy that highlights what shoppers really care about.

## Before you start
- A free DeepSeek account (sign up with an email or phone at the official site)
- A web browser on your phone or computer — about **15 minutes**
- A few notes about your product: what it is, who it's for, materials or ingredients, and one or two things that make it special

## Step 1 — Write down what you're selling
Take a minute and jot down the basics before you open anything. In plain words, write the product name, what it does or what it's made of, who it's for, and one or two things that make it different from similar products. Don't worry about being clever — you're just collecting facts for the AI to work with. A note on your phone works perfectly. **You'll know it worked when** you have at least four short facts in front of you (for example: "soy candle, lavender and vanilla, 8 oz, hand-poured in small batches, burns about 40 hours, gift-ready box").

💬 Example notes for a candle shop:
*"Lavender + vanilla soy candle, 8 oz, hand-poured, 40-hour burn, gift-ready kraft box. For people who want a calm evening after work."*

## Step 2 — Open DeepSeek and start a fresh chat
Go to DeepSeek's website in your browser. Sign in if you aren't already, then look for a **"New Chat"** button — it's usually near the top of the sidebar or at the top of the main panel. Tap or click it. A clean, empty conversation opens with a text box at the bottom and a model selector near it. **If the layout looks different on your device**, look for a pencil icon or a plus sign instead of "New Chat"; the empty conversation will appear in the same way. **You'll know it worked when** you see a blank chat with no previous messages showing.

## Step 3 — Tell DeepSeek what you sell and who it's for
In the text box at the bottom, write a short prompt that gives the AI your product details and the kind of shopper you're trying to reach. The more specific you are about the buyer, the friendlier the result. Paste in the notes from Step 1, then add a line about the audience and the length you want. **If the AI answers in a language other than English**, look for a language toggle in the settings or just write "Reply in English" at the end of your prompt. **You'll know it worked when** DeepSeek replies with a complete draft description — usually within a few seconds.

💬 Example prompt:
'Write a friendly 120-word product description for an online candle shop. Product: hand-poured soy candle, 8 oz, lavender and vanilla scent, 40-hour burn time, comes in a gift-ready kraft box. Target buyer: women 25–45 who want to unwind after a busy workday. Highlight the calm scent, the long burn, and the gift-ready packaging. Avoid flowery clichés.'*

## Step 4 — Ask for a version that leads with the benefit
Most product listings bury the best part. Ask DeepSeek to rewrite the description so the **top sentence** is the benefit a shopper cares about most — not the materials or the size. A simple follow-up works well: just tell it what to lead with. **If the rewrite still starts with the product name**, add "Start the very first sentence with how it makes the shopper feel" and ask again. **You'll know it worked when** the first sentence answers a shopper's question like "What's in this for me?" instead of just naming the product.

💬 Example follow-up:
*'Rewrite it so the first sentence is the calm-evening benefit for a tired person after work. Keep it at 120 words.'*

## Step 5 — Tighten, simplify, and remove filler
Now look at the draft with fresh eyes. Copy it into your note and ask DeepSeek to make one focused change at a time: shorter, simpler words, or fewer adjectives. For an online shop, simple words sell better than fancy ones. A prompt like "Use plain words a 12-year-old would understand" usually helps. **If the result loses the friendly tone**, add "Keep it warm and conversational — just use simpler words." **You'll know it worked when** you can read the whole description out loud in under 30 seconds and it sounds like a real person, not a brochure.

💬 Example follow-up:
*'Tighten this to about 80 words. Use plain, everyday language. Keep the warm tone. Cut any sentence that doesn't add new information.'*

## Step 6 — Ask for a short version and a quick social caption
Most shops need more than one description: a full listing for the product page and a short hook for social media or email. Ask DeepSeek for both in one go. Be clear about the word count and where each will be used — that keeps the AI from rambling. **If the social caption feels too "salesy"**, ask for a version that "reads like a tip from a friend." **You'll know it worked when** you have two pieces of copy: one polished listing for the product page, and one or two punchy sentences you can paste straight into Instagram, an email subject line, or a marketplace ad.

💬 Example prompt:
*'Give me two things: (1) the final 80-word product description for the listing, and (2) a 25-word caption I can post on Instagram that feels like a tip from a friend, not an ad.'*

## Common mistakes
- **Vague prompts give vague copy.** "Write a product description for a candle" gives generic results. Always include the materials, the audience, and the mood — that's what makes it sound like *your* product.
- **Pasting the first draft without reading it.** AI drafts are a starting point, not a finished product. Always read it out loud and fix any sentence that sounds awkward or untrue.
- **Forgetting what the AI cannot do.** DeepSeek can draft the words, but it can't check spelling in your shop platform, upload the photo, set the price, or press "publish" for you. Those last steps are yours.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** Selling handmade goods at a weekend market? Use the same workflow to write a sign card or a short pitch you can tell customers in 20 seconds.
- **For your business or work:** A clear, benefit-first description usually converts better than a feature-heavy one — and once you have a prompt that works, you can reuse it for every new product.
- **If you're just getting started:** Do this for *one* product first. The more you do, the faster it gets, and the better your prompts become.

## Try it now
Pick one product from your shop — the one you know best. Open DeepSeek, paste in your four facts, and use the prompt from Step 3. You'll have a friendly draft in under a minute, and you can polish it from there.
